item.title: THL ends milling season early amid grower payment uncertainty
item.dc:creator: Jyothi Laldas
item.description: Thousands of sugar cane growers in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) face mounting uncertainty after Tongaat Hulett Limited (THL) ended its milling season prematurely and confirmed that it would be unable to pay growers for October cane deliveries on the usual date.

item.title: Mbizana maize hub aims to process 24 000t a year
item.dc:creator: Octavia Avesca Spandiel
item.description: The Mbizana Rural Enterprise Development Hub in the Eastern Cape has procured its first 150t of WM1 maize for the 2025/25 season from an emerging farmer in Mthatha, marking the start of its commercial operations as it targets annual processing 24 000t.

item.title: Improving wheat yields: make in-season nitrogen applications count
item.dc:creator: Lindi Botha
item.description: Applying more fertiliser does not necessarily improve wheat yields or grain quality. Research shows that nutrient imbalances can prevent wheat from using the nutrients already available, leaving farmers spending money on fertiliser that may not deliver the expected results. Lindi Botha reports on how farmers can identify nutritional limitations and make more effective in-season fertiliser decisions.

item.title: Zimbabwe pays nearly 50% of BIPPA compensation
item.dc:creator: Clemence Manyukwe
item.category: Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (BIPPA)
item.description: Zimbabwe has paid nearly 50% of compensation owed to foreign farmers protected under Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (BIPPAs) who lost their properties during the country’s land reform programme, with plans to settle the outstanding amounts by 2028.

item.title: Babylonstoren’s Chianina herd focuses on quality, productivity, and animal care
item.dc:creator: Annelie Coleman
item.description: Babylonstoren’s Chianina herd is a perfect example of how farming and food can come together, from raising the cattle on the farm to serving their beef in its restaurants and offering it through the farm shop, herdmaster Kobus Lambrechts tells Annelie Coleman.
